ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, this one turns on a clock, and both advocates have read it correctly.

WHY THE FEE COMES BACK. POL-NS-10(a) runs the free cancellation grace from the moment the trip is accepted, not from the booking request, and it is not shortened by anything the driver does. Trip record EV-TRIP-02737 shows accepted_at 2026-09-15T15:07:39+08:00 and cancelled_at 2026-09-15T15:09:39+08:00 - 120 seconds - and this trip's own platform_policy carries grace_after_match_sec 180. The cancellation therefore falls inside the grace, is not chargeable whatever the driver's position, and POL-NS-10(c) directs a full refund of the fee so charged with no driver compensation. The rider's two minutes is comfortably inside the three minutes.

AMOUNT. Fare breakdown EV-FARE-02737 shows total_charged SGD 4.50, made up solely of a cancellation_fee line of SGD 4.50, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The full SGD 4.50 is refunded to the rider. driver_compensation_sgd is null: POL-NS-10(c) excludes driver compensation and POL-NS-07 is not engaged.

THE FEE IS NOT A DEFENSIBLE NO-SHOW. Both sides are right that POL-NS-01 fails. Limb (a) needs a driver 'arrived' event and there is none - arrived_at is null and the event list holds only driver_assigned, driver_en_route and trip_cancelled. Limb (d) needs termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, and the recorded code is RIDER_CANCELLED, which is none of the three. The rider's proximity points also stand: GPS trace EV-GPS-02737 puts the driver's closest approach at 6,833 m (min_distance_m) and mean distance 8,250 m, with 0 qualifying in-radius fixes, a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds and speeds of 57-62 km/h throughout - far outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and outside even the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling. POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable as well, because there are no in-geofence intervals to sum; the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02737-01 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) carries no deciding fact and its absence is adverse to neither party.

NO REFERRALS. There is no 'arrived' event and no wait-timer event, so POL-NS-05 has no marker to impugn and no false-arrival record or driver-education item is entered against this driver. POL-NS-04 does not apply: chat log EV-CHAT-02737 holds 0 messages and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so limb (a) cannot be met, and the refund rests on the clock rather than on any failure by the driver.

DRIVER PROFILE. No adverse finding is made. driver_profile EV-DPROF-02737 shows no_show_terminations_30d 0 against completed_trips_30d 113, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged. The rating, acceptance rate, account age and lifetime counters named in argument - prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags among them - are context only under POL-GEN-01 and have been used as a ground in neither direction.

CONFIDENCE AND INTEGRITY. The deciding facts are carried by trip record EV-TRIP-02737 and fare breakdown EV-FARE-02737, both COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0; the GPS trace is COMPLETE at 1.0 with 100 percent coverage and no gaps, the chat log's 0 messages reconcile with trip_record.chat_message_count 0, and the fare ledger reconciles to the cent against platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd. No artifact meets the POL-NS-08(a)-(d) impairment limbs and nothing this ruling rests on is down-weighted under POL-GEN-02, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is set at 0.95.

The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so it executes automatically on issue, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider: the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands, and no part of it is refunded. To the driver: you are paid $3.60 compensation (80% of the $4.50 fee in force); the remaining 20% is the platform's service fee.

Why the fee stands — POL-NS-01 needs all four limbs, and all four hold. (a) The trip record EV-TRIP-02736 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 13:24:34. (b) The GPS trace EV-GPS-02736 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that moment — the longest qualifying in-geofence run starts at 13:24:34 and runs 44 qualifying fixes. (c) The in-geofence dwell, measured from the first qualifying fix and not from the arrival tap, is 428 s, comfortably over the 180 s free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is not set, so no longer threshold applies). (d) No boarding occurred and the driver terminated the trip at 13:31:43 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one second after the dwell elapsed.

Nothing displaces the fee. POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver's stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, not at a wrong face of the venue. POL-NS-05 does not apply: the arrival marker was not false — the recomputed clock begins at the first qualifying in-geofence fix, which is the tapped moment itself (dwell start offset 0.0 s), so there is no false-arrival referral. POL-NS-06 gives no refund: the dwell exceeds the 180 s minimum by 248 s, so there is no shortfall, and the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02736-01 (weight 0.0) is irrelevant because no separate in-geofence intervals need to be summed. POL-NS-10 refunds nothing: the rider did not cancel and no waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee 0.00).

The rider's claim 'I was there.' does not change this. The only route by which a rider's presence or coordination defeats a no-show fee is POL-NS-04, and it fails at its first limb: the chat log EV-CHAT-02736 holds exactly one message and it is the driver's ('hi im at the pickup point', 13:24:59), so no rider locating or coordinating message exists on the record. POL-NS-04 therefore does not exonerate the rider and the fee is untouched. (Claims built on the rider device track were discarded before me for failure to disclose the GPS impairment and are not relied on here.)

Driver compensation — POL-NS-07 pays 80% of the $4.50 fee in force = $3.60 (the figure the fare ledger also computes). The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the '4 or more' limb, and 2 divided by 64 completed trips in 30 days is 0.03, below the 0.08 limb. Compensation is therefore paid, and under POL-GEN-03 the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring the $3.60 — the charge to the rider stands as it presently is (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The fee line reconciles to the fee in force ($4.50 = $4.50 net), so no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect arises.

Weight and confidence. The finding rests on the driver's in-geofence arrival and dwell, and only the GPS trace EV-GPS-02736 carries that fact. That artifact is impaired at weight 0.85 with issue code GPS_GAP_SHORT_OR_OUTSIDE_WINDOW — a 60 s sampling gap from 13:21:14 to 13:22:14. The gap lies before the waiting window opened and is under POL-NS-08(b)'s 120 s policy threshold, so it does not impair the arrival or dwell finding and the finding survives the discount; under POL-GEN-02(2), however, it caps confidence at 0.85. The trip record, chat log and fare breakdown are each at weight 1.0, and no independent artifact carries the in-geofence position fact, so the cap remains 0.85. That is above the 0.70 floor, so the case does not escalate.

No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; there is no repeat-dispute pattern between these parties; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip; and no deciding fact rests solely on an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d).

The monetary effect ($3.60) is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically. Both parties may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

This was an advance (scheduled) booking, and the cancellation fell outside the chargeable window. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02738) shows the booking accepted at 17:10:08 on 10 Aug 2026 for a scheduled pickup at 17:55:08, and the rider cancelled at 17:35:08 — 1,200 seconds before the scheduled time. The policy in force for this trip sets the advance cancellation grace at 900 seconds before the scheduled pickup (platform_policy.advance_grace_before_scheduled_sec), so the free-cancellation period ran up to 17:40:08. The rider cancelled more than 900 seconds before the scheduled time, and POL-NS-10(b) states that such a cancellation 'is not chargeable'. The trip was accepted at 17:10:08, well before that 900-second window opened, so POL-NS-10(b)'s proviso pulling limb (a) in from accepted_at does not apply, and the 180-second post-match grace of limb (a) is irrelevant. POL-NS-10(c) then directs that the fee charged on a cancellation made non-chargeable by limb (a) or (b) is refunded in full with no driver compensation: the payments ledger (EV-FARE-02738) shows cancellation_fee 4.50 SGD, total_charged 4.50 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the whole contested 4.50 SGD returns to the rider. To the driver: your reading of POL-NS-10(f) as the governing charging rule is rejected. Limb (f) charges 'a rider's own cancellation after the grace in limb (a) or (b)' — that is, one falling after the free-cancellation period has run. This cancellation was made inside the limb (b) advance grace (17:35:08, before the window opened at 17:40:08), so limb (f) is not engaged and limb (b) governs. Your remaining points are accepted as correct on the record but do not change the outcome: the driver did begin navigating 8 seconds after acceptance (17:10:16), the trace runs 157 fixes with no gaps and 100% coverage, no limb (f) refund exception is made out, and the 4.50 SGD fare line reconciles to the platform's published figure, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises. To the rider: your core case is right, and it is independently supported. The baseline no-show charge also fails: POL-NS-01 limb (a) requires a driver 'arrived' event in the trip record and there is none (arrived_at is null and the event list runs driver_assigned to driver_en_route to trip_cancelled only), and limb (d) requires termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, whereas the record closes with RIDER_CANCELLED. The driver's own trace places him about 14,000 m from the pickup pin and moving at 57–63 km/h at the moment of cancellation, so the 180-second free waiting period was never served (0 seconds of in-geofence dwell) and POL-NS-06 supports a full refund. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-01 is not satisfied on any limb, so POL-NS-07's payout condition is never reached, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the required 4, and 2/90 = 0.022, below the required 0.08), so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged. Evidence quality: the ruling rests on the trip record and the fare breakdown, both carrying weight_multiplier 1.0, and no POL-NS-08 limb is engaged (no clock skew, no trace gap over 120 seconds, the chat log is internally consistent, and the fare line reconciles), so confidence is not capped below 1.0 and is stated at 0.92. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02738-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact this ruling needs (POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is not required) and it does not affect the outcome or the confidence. No clause produces a referral and the case does not escalate: confidence 0.92 is above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect of 4.50 SGD is at or below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold, so this provisional ruling is executed automatically on issue.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both parties: this ruling concerns the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02739.

The rider is right on one point, and it does not help her. This charge cannot stand as a driver-declared no-show: POL-NS-01 limb (d) requires the trip record to show the trip terminated by the DRIVER under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. EV-TRIP-02739 shows cancelled_by RIDER, cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED and status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER at 15:20:31, with no driver termination anywhere in the event list. Limb (d) therefore fails and the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

It is chargeable under POL-NS-10, which governs a fee triggered by the rider's own cancellation. The rider accepted at 15:09:24 and cancelled at 15:20:31, 667 seconds later - far beyond the 180-second grace_after_match_sec - so POL-NS-10(f) makes the fee stand at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd = SGD 4.50. None of the four exceptions is on the record: the driver began navigating 8 seconds after assignment; he arrived at 15:14:06, inside 180 seconds of the 4-minute ETA shown to the rider at assignment; he never asked the rider to cancel; and there is no vehicle or driver mismatch. POL-NS-10(g) applies on top of that: EV-GPS-02739 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius in one continuous qualifying run of 382 seconds, from 15:14:06 to 15:20:28, comfortably exceeding the 180-second free waiting period in force (EV-TRIP-02739.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The rider cancelled after the driver had performed, and the fee stands as if the trip had been terminated for a no-show.

The rider cannot be exculpated. EV-GPS-02739's rider track places her device 764.6 m to 771.3 m from the pin (mean 767.9 m) with no qualifying fix, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed, and POL-NS-11 has no application where the rider track is present and runnable. There is no waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06: the derived shortfall is -202 seconds. The driver's 'im at the pickup' (15:14:36) was read at 15:14:56, minutes before the cancellation.

Compensation: POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force = SGD 3.60, the same figure the fare_breakdown money block computes. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 2 is below 4, and 2 divided by 101 completed_trips_30d is about 0.02, below 0.08. Lifetime counters such as prior_no_show_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not used as a ground.

Integrity and weight: every artifact carrying a deciding fact - EV-TRIP-02739, EV-GPS-02739, EV-CHAT-02739 and EV-FARE-02739 - is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The fare line of SGD 4.50 reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, satisfying POL-NS-08(d), and the trace has 100 percent coverage with no gaps. The one impaired artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02739-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no deciding fact: its absence merely makes the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation route unavailable and unnecessary.

Outcome: the disputed charge stands (POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION disposition for the fee) and the driver is compensated, so the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 3.60. The monetary effect is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold of POL-GEN-05. No referral fires: the arrival marker is genuine (dwell start offset 0.0 seconds, minimum recorded distance 0.11 m, no 15 km/h motion), so POL-NS-05(ii) has no false-arrival event to record, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming branch does not trip.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: this dispute is about the $5.00 waiting-time line on trip TRP-02740 (fare_breakdown.waiting_time_fee 5.00; platform_policy.waiting_fee_sgd 5.00), not a no-show cancellation fee. The trip was completed, and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 against total_charged 33.23. The contested amount is $5.00.

The driver's arrival is genuine, and I say so: the 'I'm Here' tap at 2026-09-03T09:11:59 is matched by 11 qualifying GPS fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius starting at the same second, with the driver stationary and the trace closing to well under a metre of the pin. POL-NS-02 is satisfied and POL-NS-05 is not met (the driver was neither more than 300 m from the pin nor moving at 15 km/h or more), so no false-arrival referral is entered against the driver.

The charge fails on its own condition. Under POL-NS-10(d) a waiting-time fee is chargeable only where the trip was completed AND the driver's in-geofence dwell before the rider boarded, measured as POL-NS-01(c) measures it (from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the arrival tap), exceeded the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec 180). It did not. The measured dwell is 100 seconds, from the first qualifying fix at 09:11:59 to the trip start at 09:13:39, giving a shortfall of 80 seconds recorded on the trace; the trip record's own wait timer (09:12:01 to 09:13:39, 98 seconds) and its wait_time_min of 1.7 minutes agree. There is only one in-geofence interval (run_count 1) and no admissible traffic advisory to permit any accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) — EV-ADVIS-02740-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), which makes limb (i) unavailable rather than excusing anything.

Both advocates' claims on these points are answered together: the driver's claims that arrival is verified, that the marker is not false, that the amount itself is the platform's published $5.00 figure and not a figure the driver selected, that no billing-integrity defect of the kind POL-NS-08(d) describes arises, that no POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance goodwill applies (a single registered pickup point, rider track within 7.4 m of the pin), and that no anti-farming pattern exists (no_show_terminations_30d 0 against completed_trips_30d 67) are all accepted. His candid concession that the 100-second dwell does not exceed the 180-second free period is correct and is what carries the outcome. The rider's claims that the platform timer, the trip record's wait_time_min and the GPS dwell all fall short of 180 seconds, that POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable, that POL-NS-12 is outside the case (arrival_marker is BUTTON and there is no wait_timer_expired event), and that the fee's condition turns only on the driver's dwell and not on the rider's conduct (rider track 241 of 241 fixes qualifying within the 100 m radius) are accepted. The refund is licensed by POL-NS-10(e), which refunds a waiting-time line the fee is not chargeable for in full; POL-GEN-07 is not reached because a clause of the policy does license the outcome.

Because the whole contested amount is returned, the ruling is FULL_REFUND of $5.00. No driver compensation arises: the free waiting period the fee is consideration for was never served, and no clause provides the driver a payment where a completed trip carries a fee the rider did not owe. No clause produces a referral.

On evidence weight (POL-GEN-02): the deciding facts — the driver's arrival, the 100-second dwell and the $5.00 line — are carried by EV-GPS-02740, EV-TRIP-02740 and EV-FARE-02740, each complete and each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and I set confidence at 0.95. EV-ADVIS-02740-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and is relied on only for that absence. No escalation applies under POL-NS-09: the artifacts do not contradict each other, no anti-farming or repeat-dispute trigger fires, nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08, and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect of $5.00 is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable. This is a refund on the clock, not a finding that the driver acted in bad faith.

The driver did arrive, and I accept that. The trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 18:33:47, 9m45s after the 18:24:02 match, and the GPS trace's arrival block records 19 qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 18:33:47 (run_count 1, no excursions, gaps [] and max_gap_sec 0.0). POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are therefore met, on a trace that is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage. The driver's claims that POL-NS-03 does not apply (his stationary fixes lie inside the radius, not outside it) and that POL-NS-05 raises no false-arrival finding (the first qualifying in-geofence fix coincides with the 'I'm Here' tap, dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0, so there is no recomputed clock and no false-arrival referral) are accepted.

The fee nonetheless fails on the waiting period. POL-NS-01(c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period in force, which is trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 s. The platform's own derived measurement gives the single qualifying run as 179.0 s, from the first qualifying fix at 18:33:47 to the termination at 18:36:46, a shortfall of 1.0 s (derived.arrival.shortfall_sec 1.0). The platform's wait-timer events corroborate independently: the free waiting period started at 18:33:49 and the trip was cancelled at 18:36:46, 177 s later. POL-NS-01(d) likewise requires termination at or after the dwell elapsed (18:36:47); the trip was terminated at 18:36:46. POL-NS-06 is drafted as strict liability: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the fee 'is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'.

I have considered and rejected the driver's argument that a 1.0 s margin below the trace's 10 s sampling interval is not proof of a shortfall. The policy provides no de minimis allowance and does not read the shortfall down to the sampling cadence; the governing measurement is the platform's own derived figure of 179.0 s, and the platform's wait-timer events (177 s) agree in direction. POL-NS-12 cannot assist the driver, because it applies only where trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO; here it is BUTTON, so limbs (b) and (c) are decided on the exported trace.

The rider's absence is accepted as fact: no boarding event is recorded, the only chat message is the driver's at 18:34:07 ('im at the pickup point', read 18:34:37), the rider sent nothing in the waiting window, and the rider's track never came within 600 m of the pin (mean 619.4 m, rider_qualifying_fix_count 0). The rider's assertion that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is not supported - the cancellation came 12m44s after the match and after a documented in-geofence wait. But the refund does not depend on the rider's presence; it follows from the shortfall itself. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider either (limb (a) needs a rider message and there is none), and the refund issues under POL-NS-06 and not under POL-NS-04.

The missing advisory EV-ADVIS-02741-01 (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no traffic_advisory is present or populated) makes POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals unavailable, but that is moot: the trace shows one in-geofence interval, so there is nothing to sum in any event.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 compensates at 80% of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-06 both withholds the fee and expressly states that no compensation is payable, so the SGD 3.60 figure carried in the fare derivation is not paid, and the driver's claim that this is a DRIVER_COMPENSATION case with amount_sgd mirroring that payout is rejected. The anti-farming check does not trip - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against completed_trips_30d of 62, a rate of 0.016, failing both limbs of that conjunctive test - so no escalation follows from it.

No escalation arises at all. Every artifact is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no POL-NS-08(a) to (d) impairment engages and no finding is discounted under POL-GEN-02; there is no direct contradiction between admissible artifacts on arrival, dwell or rider presence; disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both sides; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0.

Refund: SGD 4.50, read from fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee and total_charged (both SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), equal to platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd and reconciling with it, so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect exists. amount_sgd is the refund to the filing party; driver_compensation_sgd is null. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold (SGD 8.00), so the refund executes automatically. No clause produces a referral on these facts: the arrival marker is not false (POL-NS-05(ii)), the anti-farming check does not trip (POL-NS-07), and the reason code carried is RIDER_NO_SHOW, the rider's failure to appear, so POL-NS-01's driver-education referral for a code other than the rider's non-appearance is not engaged.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
This dispute is over the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee shown on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02742), and it turns on whether all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. They do. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:35:49. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02742) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:35:49, and it holds 19 qualifying in-radius fixes, so the arrival test of POL-NS-02 is met; the arrival marker's own timestamp coincides with that fix, so POL-NS-05 finds no false marker to correct. (c) The continuous in-geofence dwell runs from that first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 to the cancellation at 18:38:50, i.e. 181 seconds against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). POL-NS-01(c) expressly measures the dwell from the first qualifying GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' event or the platform wait timer, so the submission that the wait-timer start at 18:35:51 leaves a 179-second shortfall is declined: the wrong clock was used. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:38:50 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises, at or after the moment the dwell elapsed. The rider's other routes do not open. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to operate on, because the effective in-geofence dwell (181 s) exceeds the minimum; POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius, not in the 50-400 m wrong-entrance band; POL-NS-04 does not exonerate, because the only chat message is the driver's own, sent 18:36:09, and the rider's 46 fixes sit 622-630 m from the pin, outside the 100 m rider-presence radius. The traffic advisory that POL-NS-06(i) requires before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed is MISSING (EV-ADVIS-02742-01, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed by both sides), so no outside-radius time can be recovered - which changes nothing here, because the driver's dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run. The fee therefore stands, and POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of SGD 4.50, which is SGD 3.60. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the threshold of 4, so compensation is payable rather than withheld. Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and amount_sgd mirrors driver_compensation_sgd; the rider's charge itself is left as it stands and is not a second payment. Confidence is capped at 1.0, the weight of the GPS trace and trip record that carry the deciding facts. No clause produces a referral: the arrival marker was not false under POL-NS-05(ii), the RIDER_NO_SHOW code was correctly selected, and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met (the two-second difference between the wait-timer start and the GPS dwell start is well inside POL-NS-08(a), and POL-NS-01(c) resolves which clock governs). The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute is over the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02743 after the driver cancelled at 13:51:35 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The fee is properly chargeable and the driver is owed SGD 3.60.

Why the fee stands (POL-NS-01, read from EV-TRIP-02743, EV-GPS-02743 and EV-FARE-02743). All four limbs hold: (a) the trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 13:45:32; (b) the GPS trace places him inside the arrival geofence for this STANDARD pickup — 37 qualifying fixes (accuracy within 25 m) inside the 50 m radius, the first at 13:45:32, which is the 'arrived' timestamp POL-NS-01(b) requires; (c) he then held position inside that radius in one continuous run of 360 seconds, from 13:45:32 to 13:51:32 — double the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec); and (d) the record shows no boarding and a driver termination at 13:51:35 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises, more than three minutes after the required dwell elapsed at 13:48:32. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the fee.

To the rider on your points. You are right that the driver stopped a short distance from the pin, and the trace bears you out: his closest approach was 41.4 m. But the policy measures arrival by the arrival radius, and 41.4 m is inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, so POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance) — which applies only where the driver's stationary fixes are outside the radius — does not apply, and your account that he 'parked a bit away' does not defeat limb (b). Your own rider track is strong (66 qualifying fixes, 16.3–23.6 m from the pin, stationary from 13:42:45 to after the cancellation; POL-NS-04 limb (c) is met), but POL-NS-01 does not make proof of your absence a condition of the fee — limb (d) reads only the reason code and the absence of a boarding event. The clause that protects a rider who is present and trying to coordinate is POL-NS-04, and it needs all three limbs. Limb (a) fails: your only message in the window is 'ok' at 13:47:02, which is an acknowledgement and none of the things limb (a) lists — not your own position, not an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, not a request for the driver's position, and not a statement that you could not see the vehicle. Limb (b) is met (the driver posted no reply within 120 seconds and made no in-app call) and so is limb (c), but with limb (a) unmet the clause cannot refund the fee. Your point about the missing traffic advisory is taken: EV-ADVIS-02743-01 is MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0, so no aggregation of separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is available to either side — but nothing turns on it, because the driver's 360-second run already exceeds the 180-second minimum on its own and there is no shortfall to aggregate.

To the driver on your points. POL-NS-05 does not fire: at 13:45:32 the trace places you 41.4 m from the pin and stationary at 0 km/h, so neither the 300 m trigger nor the 15 km/h trigger fires, your marker is not false, and no false-arrival referral is recorded. Your statement that you were 'right at the pin' is not exactly what the trace shows, but the geofence test is what governs and it is satisfied. POL-NS-07 then fixes your payout at 80 percent of the net fee in force: 80% x SGD 4.50 = SGD 3.60, the figure the fare ledger computes (EV-FARE-02743). The anti-farming check does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2/123 = 0.016 (below 0.08) — so compensation is paid.

Outcome, confidence and execution. The rider's charge of SGD 4.50 stands unchanged (the fee disposition is NO_ACTION), and because compensation is payable the emitted ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd carrying the same SGD 3.60 as driver_compensation_sgd (POL-GEN-03). Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — EV-TRIP-02743, EV-GPS-02743 and EV-FARE-02743 — is at weight 1.0, so no discount applies under POL-GEN-02 and the MISSING advisory carried no deciding fact. Confidence 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; no ground under POL-NS-09 applies, so there is no escalation. The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically under POL-GEN-05. This is a provisional ruling made without human review and either party may appeal it under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

Rider and driver: this dispute is decided on the record, without a human reviewer.

Outcome. The $4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged to the rider stands and is not refunded, and the driver is paid $3.60 compensation.

Why the fee stands — POL-NS-01 requires four things, and all four are on the record. (a) The trip record carries the driver's own 'arrived' event at 18:06:05 on 17 Aug 2026. (b) The exported GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at that moment: 41 fixes qualify, the closest 0.16 m from the pin, well beyond the three consecutive accuracy-filtered in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires. (c) He held position in one continuous run of 400 seconds, from 18:06:05 to 18:12:45, against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) — a surplus of 220 seconds. (d) He terminated the trip at 18:12:48 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event, which is after the required dwell elapsed. The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: at 18:06:05 the driver was 0.16 m from the pin and stationary, not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or above, so the waiting clock legitimately runs from that fix.

What each side argued. The rider is right that POL-NS-12 cannot assist the driver here — this trip's arrival marker is a driver-pressed BUTTON, and POL-NS-12 covers only GPS_AUTO arrivals. That point is accepted but immaterial, because the POL-NS-02 geofence test is satisfied on the exported trace itself. The rider is also right that POL-NS-06 does not open: 400 seconds is a surplus against the 180-second minimum, not a shortfall, so no refund flows from premature cancellation. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: the only message in the chat log is the driver's, sent 18:06:25, so the rider sent no locating or coordinating message and limb (a) fails. POL-NS-03 does not apply either — the driver's stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, not outside it but within 400 m — so this is not a wrong-entrance case. The driver's alternative reference to the 300-second fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec does not govern a record that carries platform_policy, as this one does; the governing minimum is 180 seconds, and 400 seconds clears either figure.

Rider's own position. The rider's device recorded 71 stationary fixes averaging about 788 m from the pin, outside the 100 m rider-presence radius. That reading is not disputed and is not used against the rider: the rider's distance is not an element of the charge, which turns on the driver's arrival, dwell and cancellation. It simply means POL-NS-04 cannot help him.

The missing traffic advisory. EV-ADVIS-02745-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and, under POL-GEN-02, can carry no fact; the absence is itself noted. It is not needed here: the driver's 400-second hold was one unbroken run, so no accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is required.

Driver's pay. POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's compensation at 80 per cent of the $4.50 fee in force — $3.60, the net figure, which is also what the fare ledger computes. The anti-farming check does not trip: one no-show termination in the trailing 30 days (below 4) at a rate of 0.008 (below 0.08), and both limbs must hold. The ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd carries the same $3.60 as the compensation figure; the rider's own $4.50 charge is unaffected and the two are not netted.

Evidence quality and confidence. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0: the 10-second trace at 100 per cent coverage with zero gaps and both tracks present, the causally ordered trip record, the chat log with intact sequence numbering, and the ledger reconciling to $4.50. No POL-NS-08(a) to (d) impairment applies, no artifact below 1.0 carries a deciding fact, and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger fires, so confidence is 0.95. The money effect of $3.60 is below the $8.00 execution threshold and is executed automatically. No clause of this policy directs a referral on these facts, so none is issued.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute is about the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02744 after the driver cancelled at 08:17:36 under the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW.

The fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. Two of them fail on the driver's own evidence. Condition (b) requires the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02744) to place the driver inside the pickup geofence, which POL-NS-02 sets at 50 m for this STANDARD pickup (trip_record.pickup_zone_class in EV-TRIP-02744): at least three consecutive fixes inside 50 m, each accurate to 25 m or better. That trace is COMPLETE, 98 fixes at a 10-second cadence with no gaps, and the derived count of qualifying in-radius fixes is 0; the driver's closest approach anywhere in the trace is 53.84 m. Condition (c) requires an in-geofence dwell of at least the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180), measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix; that dwell is 0 seconds. The 'I'm Here' button press at 08:11:35 does not start that clock: POL-NS-01(c) runs it from the GPS fix, and POL-NS-12, which lets the platform's own arrival and wait-timer events stand in for the trace, applies only where trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO, and here it is BUTTON. The six-minute wait timer therefore records a tap, not an arrival, and there is no reading of the trace on which this fee is earned.

POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) is not established either way and I make no finding under it. The derived facts report no distance and no speed for the driver at the 08:11:35 marker, so the clause's trigger - more than 300 m from the pin, or 15 km/h or more, at the marker's timestamp - cannot be tested. The 53.84 m figure the Driver Advocate relies on is the minimum across the whole trace, not the position at the marker; it is well inside POL-NS-05's 300 m leash, but it neither proves nor disproves a false marker at 08:11:35. Because no false-arrival finding is made, no POL-NS-05(ii) referral is recorded; a referral exists only where a clause produces one.

On the Driver Advocate's submission that this is a POL-NS-03 wrong-position case: accepted to this extent. A closest approach of 53.84 m lies outside the 50 m radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, so on the driver's own account he came to the venue and held just outside the radius rather than never arriving. That does not change the money. POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full, and its only two compensation routes are closed on this record. Route (i) needs the rider to have given the correct entrance, block, tower or bay in the chat log and the driver not to have moved to it, and the chat (EV-CHAT-02744) holds only the driver's 'here' at 08:11:55 and the rider's 'ok' at 08:13:05 - no sub-location from either party. Route (ii) needs trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and this trip registers exactly 1. The Rider Advocate reached the same conclusion in the alternative, and it is right. Switching to POL-NS-02 makes no difference: where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before the cancellation, the driver never arrived, limb (b) fails, and the fee is refunded in full. Both routes land on a full refund and neither produces driver compensation, so the choice between them does not affect the outcome.

Under POL-NS-06 the same result follows from the arithmetic: the effective dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second minimum, so the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages. The one route by which the driver could have accumulated separate in-geofence intervals - POL-NS-06(i) - is closed: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02744-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, payload null), and the clause makes limb (i) unavailable where the advisory is missing. There is therefore no lawful-holding excuse and no accumulation.

POL-NS-04 does not need to be reached, and it does not exonerate the rider: her only message, 'ok' at 08:13:05, names no position, entrance, block, tower or bay, asks for the driver's position, and does not say she cannot see the vehicle, so limb (a) fails at its first requirement. That does not matter, because the refund follows from the driver's trace, not from this clause. The Rider Advocate's further point that the rider was at the pickup point throughout is factually supported - EV-GPS-02744's rider_presence block shows 69 fixes, every one qualifying, all stationary, never more than 13.59 m from the pin - and it sits badly with a RIDER_NO_SHOW termination, but the fee falls on the driver's own trace test and I rest nothing on it. The driver's statement in the dispute record that he 'was right at the pin' carries no weight_multiplier, is contradicted by his own trace, and is not used as a carrier of any fact.

Driver compensation is not payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies; neither does, and POL-NS-06 displaces the fee, so the 80 per cent payout of SGD 3.60 the Driver Advocate computes is conditional on a premise that fails. For completeness, the anti-farming check does not trip on the two figures the clause names - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 required, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 91 is a rate of 0.022, below the 0.08 threshold - but that is not reached, because compensation is not owed in the first place. Those are the only profile fields used, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

Amount and integrity. EV-FARE-02744 carries a single SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line and nothing else: total_charged is 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the whole of the contested SGD 4.50 is the cancellation fee itself and the rider's success on that line is a full refund of it, not a partial one. That line equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d): the arrived event and the nearest fix agree within 10 seconds, the trace has no gaps across 98 fixes, the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 2, and the fare reconciles. Every artifact this ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing is discounted. Escalation is not engaged: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival in a way no clause resolves (POL-NS-01(b) and POL-NS-02 settle that question, and the driver accepts limb (b) fails on the trace), the parties' 90-day counterparty dispute counts are both 0, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence.

Ruling. The rider's claim is supported: FULL_REFUND of the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee, with no driver compensation. No clause of the policy in force produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty. Confidence is 0.95, within the 1.0 cap set by the two weight-1.0 artifacts, EV-GPS-02744 and EV-TRIP-02744, that carry the deciding facts, and above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the refund executes on issue.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee cannot stand, and it is returned to the rider in full. Why. Under POL-NS-01 a no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions hold. The first three are satisfied on the driver's own evidence: the trip record (EV-TRIP-02747) carries the driver's 'I'm Here' event at 11:22:26, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02747) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius of the Serangoon Ave 3 pin from 11:22:26 to 11:28:46 — 380 continuous seconds across 39 qualifying fixes, minimum distance to the pin 0.0 m — so limb (b) and the 180-second free-waiting dwell in limb (c) (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) are met, and the marker is not a false one (POL-NS-05 is not engaged: no marker more than 300 m out, no motion at or above 15 km/h). The full SGD 4.50 is returned. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the refund executes automatically. Driver compensation is nil. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full; limb (d) fails, so there is no payout. The anti-farming check does not trip in any event: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the four-or-more limb, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 138 is 0.0145, below the 0.08 rate limb. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged: both disputes_with_counterparty_90d counters are 0, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and no impaired artifact carries a deciding fact. Claims answered. The driver's claims that POL-NS-02 arrival is made out, that the marker is not false under POL-NS-05, and that the 380-second dwell exceeds the free waiting period so POL-NS-06 yields no refund on shortfall grounds are accepted — they are correct and I rely on the trace for exactly those facts — but they do not change the result, because limb (d) independently fails, which the driver's own final claim also concedes. The rider's POL-NS-04 claim (locating message 'at the lift lobby' at 11:23:26 unanswered within 120 s, no in-app call, rider device 13.1–19.1 m from the pin across 65 fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius) is also made out on EV-CHAT-02747 and EV-GPS-02747, but it is not needed: the refund follows from POL-NS-01 alone. The rider's claims that POL-NS-03 pin-ambiguity goodwill does not arise (correct — the qualifying fixes lie inside the radius, so the wrong-entrance route is not reached), that the contested sum is SGD 4.50, and that no artifact is impaired are accepted. Impaired or absent evidence. EV-ADVIS-02747-01 (traffic advisory) is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact and is not needed, because the driver's dwell was one continuous in-geofence interval, so POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation rule — the only limb that requires an advisory — never comes into play. All other artifacts (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger and both profiles) are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence in this ruling is not capped below 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.50 RIDER_NO_SHOW cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and the driver is paid nothing. Here is why.

Chargeability (POL-NS-01). The fee stands only if all four limbs hold. Limb (a) holds: the platform record shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:24:42. Limbs (b) and (c) fail. POL-NS-02 deems the driver arrived only where the gps_trace holds at least three consecutive fixes, each accurate to 25 m or better, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius of the pickup pin. The derived arrival analysis of EV-GPS-02746 (weight 1.0; 71 fixes, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0) reports qualifying_fix_count 0, run_count 0, no runs, and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds. With no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere, the driver never arrived and limb (b) fails; the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; POL-NS-01(c)), so POL-NS-06 makes the fee not chargeable. POL-NS-06 refunds a shortfall whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, so the fact that the rider's own track places the rider about 838 m from the pin throughout 09:22:37-09:31:58 is not a reason to keep the fee (it would also defeat POL-NS-04 limb (c), whose 100 m rider-presence radius is nowhere met and which no rider message could have invoked anyway).

The driver's side. The 'arrived' tap and the 399-second wait timer (09:24:44 to 09:31:23), and wait_time_min 6.7, are recorded, but POL-NS-01(c) measures dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 'arrived' event. POL-NS-12, which would treat platform arrival and wait-timer events as a carrier independent of the exported trace, does not apply because platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO. The timer therefore records only that the driver's own tap started it. The observation that derived.driver_track.min_distance_m is 0.0 while qualifying_fix_count is 0 does not rescue the arrival: POL-NS-02 provides that fixes failing the 25 m accuracy screen (and fixes of unknown accuracy) are ignored and count as evidence of neither presence nor absence, and one filtered or isolated at-pin fix cannot make the three-consecutive-qualifying-fix test. The driver's in-app message 'im at the pickup point' at 09:25:02 and the counterparty statement that he was at the pin for over six minutes are not corroborated by any derived fact and do not establish the GPS-measured arrival or dwell.

Compensation (POL-NS-07). The driver's payout is due only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; it is not satisfied, so the SGD 3.60 (80% of SGD 4.50) computed in the fare record has no basis and the retained SGD 0.90 is not owed either. On the POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance route the refund is likewise full and the driver gets no goodwill, because trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1 (not 2 or more) and the rider named no entrance, block or bay. The anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 1 against the count of 4, and 1/126 = 0.008 against the 0.08 rate), but that only removes a bar to compensation; it does not create any.

Escalation is not engaged. There is no cross-artifact contradiction the policy leaves unresolved: POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-05 expressly contemplate a wait record the trace does not support and direct that dwell be read from the trace, so POL-NS-09(b) is not met. The trace is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a)-(d): max_gap_sec 0.0, 100% coverage, the chat log holds 1 message matching trip_record.chat_message_count 1, and the SGD 4.50 fare line reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd. Both counterparty-dispute counts are 0 and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) do not fire. The only artifact below weight 1.0 is EV-ADVIS-02746-01 (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0): its absence makes POL-NS-06(i) accumulation unavailable, but no deciding fact rests on it, so it neither caps confidence nor escalates the case.

Confidence. The deciding fact - the zero in-geofence dwell shortfall - is carried by EV-GPS-02746 at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is 0.85.

Open question for the record (not a referral): the brief does not give the driver's position or speed at the 09:24:42 marker, so POL-NS-05's specific distance/speed test cannot be run and no false-arrival referral is made. No clause produces a referral on these facts, so referrals is empty.

Execution. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the POL-GEN-05 threshold of SGD 8.00 and will be executed automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04; no safety or complaint flag applies.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — the SGD 4.50 no-show fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

The cancellation was made by the driver at 19:15:10 under reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE (EV-TRIP-02748). POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four of its limbs hold, and limb (d) recognises only RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. The clause states in terms that DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE — the driver's own statement that he could not find the rider — does not satisfy limb (d). Limb (d) therefore fails, and the SGD 4.50 fee line on EV-FARE-02748 (payment status CHARGED, refund issued SGD 0.00) is not chargeable. The same clause then fixes the consequence by geography: where the driver's stationary fixes lie INSIDE the arrival radius this is a full refund of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation, and that is what the driver's own trace shows. POL-NS-03 does not apply, because that clause governs fixes outside the radius but within 400 m, and POL-NS-02's 'never arrived' branch would require fixes more than 400 m away.

For the driver. What your record does establish is accepted, and it does not save the charge. You arrived at 19:11:48 (EV-TRIP-02748), inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at the same second with a dwell start offset of 0.0 s. You held position for a continuous 200 seconds over 21 qualifying fixes, 19:11:48 to 19:15:08, against the 180-second free waiting period in force (platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so there is no POL-NS-06 shortfall (derived shortfall -20.0 s). The 'I'm Here' marker was not false under POL-NS-05: the trace placed you inside the radius at that second and you were stationary (nearest approach 0.44 m), not travelling at 15 km/h or more, so no false-arrival referral arises. The money is sound: the SGD 4.50 line reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd (4.50) and the schedule default, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The trade-off the policy makes is that a correctly waited pickup recorded under the wrong reason code is still not chargeable; your own claim on this point does not press the fee and claims no POL-NS-07 payout, and it is right.

For the rider. Independently of limb (d), POL-NS-04 exonerates you on all three limbs: you sent a locating message inside the waiting window ('at the lift lobby', 19:12:48, EV-CHAT-02748); the driver posted no reply within 120 seconds of it and made no in-app call before cancelling at 19:15:10; and your device stayed inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius on 40 of 40 fixes, maximum 19.67 m (EV-GPS-02748). Full refund, no driver compensation.

Confidence is not reduced by POL-GEN-02(2). The deciding facts rest on artifacts all at weight 1.0: the reason code and timestamps on EV-TRIP-02748, the in-radius dwell and rider presence on EV-GPS-02748, the chat on EV-CHAT-02748 and the fee line on EV-FARE-02748. No POL-NS-08 limb is met (100% coverage, no gaps, chat sequence intact, fare reconciles), so the cap is 1.0. EV-ADVIS-02748-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but it carries no deciding fact here — the dwell was a single in-geofence interval, so the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation rule that needs a traffic advisory is not in issue — and it is named in the discarded-claim audit below. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged (no profile counter in play reaches its test, and no two artifacts contradict each other), so the case is not escalated.

The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, which does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so the refund executes automatically on issue.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

The code was mis-selected and should be corrected for this driver.

ruling.explanation:

DRV-09751 accepted at 22:22:34, tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:31:15, and the GPS trace independently places him inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius from that same second, holding position for one continuous 408-second run (42 qualifying fixes) until 22:38:03 — well past the 180-second free waiting period in force. The driver cancelled at 22:38:07 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, no boarding event is recorded, and the rider's own device track never came closer than 851 m to the pin. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) are therefore satisfied and the SGD 4.50 fee would normally stand, with SGD 3.60 (80% of the fee) paid to the driver under POL-NS-07.

That payout is displaced by the driver's own profile, on a check the driver's advocate properly conceded. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming test requires both limbs and both are met: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 4 (the '4 or more' limb) and 4 divided by completed_trips_30d of 40 is 0.10, above the 0.08 rate limb. Where both limbs hold, compensation is WITHHELD and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). I tested and set aside the routes either side raised. POL-NS-06: the measured dwell of 408 seconds exceeds the 180-second minimum, the derived shortfall is −228 seconds (a surplus), so no waiting-period refund arises; the absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02751-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is irrelevant to a dwell that needs no accumulation. POL-NS-05: the arrival marker is true — the fix at the marker shares the timestamp 22:31:15 and the driver is stationary, not the 300 m or 15 km/h that would make it false. POL-NS-04: the only message in the waiting window is the driver's own, so the rider sent nothing locating or coordinating and limb (a) fails — no rider exoneration. POL-NS-12 does not apply because the arrival marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO, so the arrival rests on the exported trace, which fully supports it. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius. No artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08 (zero-second gap, no clock skew, chat count reconciles to the trip record, fare line reconciles to platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd), and every deciding fact rests on weight-1.0 records, so confidence is not capped below the floor; escalation is triggered by POL-NS-09(d), not by low confidence. I did not use rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate or the lifetime counters prior_no_show_flags / prior_disputes_filed on either party: POL-GEN-01 makes them context only, and the only profile counters that decide anything here are the two POL-NS-07 names. ruling.explanation:
Dear Rider and Driver — the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02750 is refunded in full to the rider. No compensation is payable to the driver.

Why the charge fails. The failure is on the waiting clock, not on whether the driver reached the pin. He did reach it: EV-GPS-02750 shows 80 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100.0% coverage and no gaps, of which 16 qualify (accuracy 25 m or better) inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, in a single interval from 10:43:10 to 10:45:40, with a whole-track minimum distance of 0.33 m from the pin. But POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and NOT from the 'arrived' tap, and that interval is 150 seconds long. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The dwell is 30 seconds short — the figure the derived block itself records — so POL-NS-06 makes the fee not chargeable and refunds it in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The driver's submission that the 120 seconds between the tap and the first qualifying fix should be treated as neutral does not help: POL-NS-06(i) could only add separate intervals, there is only one in-geofence interval, and the traffic advisory that limb (i) requires is MISSING (EV-ADVIS-02750-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so limb (i) is unavailable and nothing in it assists him.

The early arrival marker. The driver's own statement — 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin' — is accepted as an admission that the marker was pressed before he was at the pin, and the trace agrees: the first qualifying in-geofence fix comes 120 seconds after the 10:41:10 tap, and the driver's 10:41:30 message 'im at the pickup point' is 100 seconds before that first qualifying fix. POL-NS-05's arithmetic trigger (more than 300 m from the pin, or 15 km/h or more, at the marker's timestamp) cannot be measured from the derived block, so the marker is not recorded as a false-arrival event; and the point would not change the money, because POL-NS-05(i) — the limb that applies where a recomputed clock falls short — also refunds the fee in full with no compensation. The rider's request for a false-arrival referral is refused: POL-NS-05(ii) and (iii), which are the limbs that carry that referral, do not apply, because the trace DOES contain a qualifying in-geofence interval (so limb (ii) does not fire) and the corrected dwell does NOT meet the minimum (so limb (iii) does not fire). The reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW was correctly selected, so POL-NS-01's driver-education referral for a mis-selected code is not engaged either.

For the driver. The tribunal accepts that you came to the pin and held position there, and that limb (d) is satisfied on the record — RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three codes that limb recognises, with no boarding event and a null started_at. That is why this is a refund and not a finding that you fabricated an arrival. But POL-NS-07 pays you only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-06 displaces it here, so the 3.60 (80 per cent of 4.50) that the fare ledger's money block computes is not payable. The anti-farming check would not have withheld it in any event: 1 no-show termination against 129 completed trips in 30 days is neither 4 or more nor a rate above 0.08. POL-NS-12 cannot rescue the clock: this trip's arrival_marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO, and there is no wait_timer_expired event. POL-NS-03 does not apply either, because the driver's qualifying stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, not outside it.

For the rider. Your own evidence does not help you, and you do not need it. The rider track in EV-GPS-02750 places your device 735.7 to 742.8 m from the pin throughout the window, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed; and the chat log holds only the driver's message, so limbs (a) and (b) — which require a locating or coordinating message FROM you — are not met. POL-NS-04 therefore does not exonerate you, and POL-NS-11 is not reached (your track is present and its fixes are not filtered for accuracy). But POL-NS-06 refunds the fee regardless of your presence, so the outcome is the same.

Amount and integrity. The fare record is clean: the 4.50 cancellation-fee line reconciles with the 4.50 in force, total_charged is 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and there is no basis for splitting the amount. No two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the 90-day counterparty-dispute counters are 0 on both profiles; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0; and the anti-farming check does not trip — so there is no escalation under POL-NS-09 and the fee is not held pending review. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the 8.00 execution threshold and is released on issue.

Confidence. The facts that decide the case — the 150-second dwell and the 180-second period in force — are carried by EV-GPS-02750 and EV-TRIP-02750, both at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and no discount applies; confidence is set at 0.90.

At most 2 of 4 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.

To the rider and the driver: this dispute is decided on the trip's own evidence, and the outcome is that the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands as charged and the driver is paid the platform's 80% share, $3.60.

Why the fee stands. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four parts of POL-NS-01 hold. They do. (a) The trip record (EV-TRIP-02752, weight 1.0) carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 22:06:11. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02752, weight 1.0) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at and after that moment: 44 accuracy-qualifying fixes in one unbroken in-geofence run opening at 22:06:11, with a closest approach of 0.0 m and POL-NS-02's three-consecutive-fix test met. The STANDARD zone class is read from the trip record, not assumed. (c) That single run lasts 434 seconds (22:06:11 to 22:13:25), comfortably above the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies) — a surplus of 254 seconds. The dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not the tap, and the two are the same second (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0). (d) There is no boarding (started_at and ended_at are null) and the driver terminated at 22:13:25 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the required dwell elapsed at 22:09:11.

POL-NS-05 is not engaged: the arrival tap coincides with the first in-geofence fix, so the trace does not put the driver more than 300 m from the pin or moving at 15 km/h at the marker; there is no false arrival and no false-arrival referral.

The rider's routes were each tested and each fails. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to refund — the dwell exceeds the minimum by 254 seconds (the cited advisory limb is irrelevant, and in any case no advisory covers this pickup). POL-NS-02 / POL-NS-12: the arrival marker is a driver BUTTON press, not GPS_AUTO, so the platform's timing events do not substitute for the export — but the export itself carries the arrival and the dwell, so the limb is met on the trace. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: the chat log (EV-CHAT-02752) holds a single message and it is the driver's ('im at the pickup point', 22:06:31), so limb (a) fails; and the rider's own track places the rider's device 866–874 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m radius, so limb (c) affirmatively fails. Rider position is not an element of POL-NS-01, so this neither establishes nor defeats the charge. The filed words 'cancelled on me again' find no support in the record: rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both counterparty-dispute counters are 0.

Driver compensation. POL-NS-07 sets the payout at 80% of the $4.50 net cancellation fee in force = $3.60; the rider's gross figure ($6.61) is not used. The anti-farming check does not trip and requires both limbs: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3 (below 4) and 3 / 40 completed_trips_30d = 0.075 (below 0.08). The driver's lifetime prior_no_show_flags of 7 is not the field POL-NS-07 reads and has been given no weight whatever. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the fee, so the charge stands (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) and the case produces DRIVER_COMPENSATION; per POL-GEN-03 the amount_sgd field carries the same $3.60, being the money this ruling moves.

Integrity, escalation and execution. No POL-NS-08 impairment applies: there is no clock skew (arrival, dwell and termination timestamps agree across the trip record and the trace), no trace gap (100% coverage, 0 s maximum gap, 100 fixes, both tracks present), no chat defect (1 message matches trip_record.chat_message_count) and no fare defect (the $4.50 fare line equals the $4.50 in force). No POL-NS-09 trigger is present, so the case does not escalate. The only artifact below full weight is the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02752-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); it carries no fact for either party and does not affect this outcome. The monetary effect ($3.60) is below the $8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so the ruling executes automatically, and either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

Both sides in substance accepted that this record shows a verified no-show, and it does. For the driver: the BUTTON arrival marker means POL-NS-12 does not apply, but that does not weaken your case, because arrival and dwell are independently established by the GPS record. No clause produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty. The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically. Ruling for the rider: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee is refunded in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

The fee nevertheless fails on the waiting period. ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The trip mechanics themselves are not in dispute, and on them the driver is right. DRV-09755 tapped 'arrived' at 09:14:14 (EV-TRIP-02755), and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02755, weight 1.0, COMPLETE, 10-second cadence, no gaps) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same second, with 40 qualifying fixes. He then held position continuously for 390 seconds — against the 180-second free waiting period this trip's own platform_policy carries — and terminated at 09:20:47 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, more than three minutes after the required dwell had elapsed. That satisfies all four limbs of POL-NS-01 (arrival event, GPS proximity, dwell, reason code and timing). POL-NS-05 does not bite: the first qualifying fix is at the marker's own timestamp, the driver was stationary at the pin (min distance 0 m) and never at speed on the arrival timestamp, so the marker is genuine and the waiting clock needs no recomputation. POL-NS-06 gives no refund — the shortfall is negative, 390 s against 180 s, recorded as -210 s. POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-04 do not apply: the driver was inside the radius, not at a wrong face of the venue, and the only chat message is the driver's own 'im here' with no locating message from the rider, so POL-NS-04 limb (a) fails (its limb (c) also fails on the rider's track, which shows no qualifying fix within 100 m). POL-NS-10's grace windows are long past (cancellation about 14 minutes after acceptance, on an unscheduled trip). The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02755) reconciles to the $4.50 fee in force, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect, and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. EV-ADVIS-02755-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact and nothing here rests on it. Standing alone, this would be a verified rider no-show and POL-NS-07 would pay the driver 80% of $4.50 = $3.60, the anti-farming check not tripping (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, below 4; 2/110 = 0.018, below 0.08). But the case does not stand alone. POL-NS-09(c) sends a case to human review where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. Both read 2 (EV-RPROF-02755 and EV-DPROF-02755, each at weight 1.0) for this same pair, RDR-09755 and DRV-09755 on TRP-02755, and the rider's filing describes this as the third such cancellation and charge. That trigger is aimed at repeat behaviour a single-trip view cannot fairly assess, and it fires. I reject the driver's contrary argument (made under POL-GEN-01) insofar as it says the profile counters can never support an escalation: POL-GEN-01 expressly lists disputes_with_counterparty_90d on both profiles as citable for this test; what it excludes is the lifetime counters (prior_no_show_flags) and the rider's bare assertion of a 'pattern', neither of which I have used. Because POL-NS-09 escalation is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, replaces the ruling, no money moves now: the $4.50 disputed cancellation fee is placed on hold — not collected and not refunded — and the driver's compensation is not paid pending review. This is not a finding for either side. The question for the reviewer is whether the repeated rider/driver history (2 recorded counterparty disputes in 90 days, with the rider alleging a third) warrants anything different from the verified single-trip outcome, and the case summary goes to that reviewer with both briefs, the admissibility report, the clauses relied on and this reasoning. No referral clause fires: POL-NS-05's false-arrival record is not engaged (the marker was genuine) and POL-NS-07's anti-farming branch does not trip. Confidence is 0.90: the escalation rests on two independent weight-1.0 profile artifacts, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0, above the 0.70 floor; and the amount is held in any event.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02757 (EV-FARE-02757: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded to the rider in full.

The charge was raised on a cancellation the rider herself made, so POL-NS-10 governs. She cancelled at 21:44:13, 420 seconds after the 21:37:13 acceptance on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02757), which is outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec. Standing alone that makes the fee chargeable under POL-NS-10(f) whether or not the driver had arrived, and the driver is right that three of the four exceptions are not engaged: the driver did begin moving toward the pickup at 21:37:21, inside the grace; the only ETA shown was 15 minutes from assignment (21:52:13), and the rider cancelled at 21:44:13, before it; and no driver or vehicle mismatch is recorded.

The third exception is engaged, however, and POL-NS-10(f) is disjunctive — any single exception refunds the fee in full. The chat log EV-CHAT-02757 (weight_multiplier 1.0, no issue codes) records the driver's message MSG-02757-001 sent 21:41:13 — 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side' — which the rider answered 'ok cancelling' at 21:42:13 and then cancelled. That is the driver asking the rider to cancel, on the chat_log, exactly as the exception requires; the driver advocate concedes it.

Independently the driver never arrived, so POL-NS-10(g) — which would let the fee stand despite limb (f) where the driver had arrived and served the free waiting period — cannot apply. The trip record carries no 'arrived' event (arrived_at null; events only driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled), so POL-NS-01 limb (a) fails. The record was closed under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED with cancelled_by RIDER, not one of the three no-show codes, so limb (d) fails. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02757 (weight 1.0) yields 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes with a nearest approach of 7,000.01 m against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so limb (b) fails under POL-NS-02, and POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling is nowhere near met. POL-NS-06 independently refunds: effective in-geofence dwell 0 s against the 180 s free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a 180 s shortfall. The MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02757-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact; it only makes POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation limb unavailable, and there are no in-geofence intervals to sum in any event.

Driver compensation: none. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the charge; POL-NS-01 fails and POL-NS-06 displaces it. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against completed_trips_30d 104 (rate 0.019), so the anti-farming check does not trip and there is no POL-NS-09 escalation.

Confidence: 0.95. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the chat log, the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; the only artifact below 1.0 is the absent advisory at 0.0, which carries no fact. That is above the 0.70 escalation floor.

Referrals: none. No clause produces one — POL-NS-05's false-arrival record is not engaged because no arrival marker was ever pressed, and POL-NS-07's escalation packet is not triggered.

The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so this refund is executed automatically. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
