The driver's submission that POL-RD-09 adds nothing is accepted; there is no unmatched charge line, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral fires either. The rider's claim that the refund would be a partial rather than a full refund is accepted on the figures, but it does not change the outcome, because escalation replaces the monetary ruling altogether.

THE OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER, which belongs here rather than in referrals: the computed refund sits just SGD 15.92 above the SGD 150.00 escalation ceiling, and the reviewer should consider whether the ceiling is the right disposition on these figures or whether the optimal route should be re-quoted on a record-type artifact. Outcome: the rider's claim is not made out and the fare stands. Both of you should read the two figures that decide it. This was a pooled trip (vehicle_type RYDE_POOL), and for pooled trips POL-RD-12 fixes the comparison at the matched-itinerary distance the platform computed at match time, read from trip_record.optimal_distance_km = 16.0 km ('matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider'). The 11.5 km in the rider's complaint is the separate solo_optimal_distance_km field, carried for reference only; a claim measured against it fails on that ground alone, and the rider's advocate rightly did not press it. Distance spent collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation, and the driver's account of the co-rider pickup is corroborated by the trip record itself, not merely asserted.

Measured against the matched itinerary, the overrun is 0.96 km: 16.96 km on the GPS trace less 16.0 km. The trace figure governs over trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.0 km, which POL-RD-01 treats as a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH more than 20% of the optimal distance AND more than 0.8 km absolute. The 0.96 km does clear the absolute limb, but 20% of 16.0 km is 3.2 km, and 0.96 km is 6.00%. The relative limb fails, both limbs must pass, and no route deviation is established. POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION in that event, save for a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4), to which I turn below.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 does not run and no fare recomputation issues. For transparency only: on these figures it would have produced a recomputed fare of $22.76 against the $23.51 charged, a $0.75 refund before rounding, but the clause applies only where POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation. POL-RD-09 gives nothing either. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines (0.00, erp_gantries empty), no airport surcharge (0.00) on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and no promo or waiting-time anomaly. The distance line billed at 17.0 km matches the trace's 16.96 km within round convention, so it is not a phantom line and there is no unmatched charge line in the ledger. No POL-RD-09(4) finding arises and no referral follows.

The GPS trace is clean at policy level: 133 fixes, 100.0% coverage, a 10-second sampling interval, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) do not fire and no impaired-trace handling or POL-RD-10(3) escalation applies. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02860-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 could not have been run had a closure been asserted; no traffic cause was in fact asserted by either party, and the driver's answer rests on the pooled baseline in the trip record. The chat log carries zero messages and both amendment timestamps are null, so POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-05 have nothing to operate on. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, and no clause produces a referral.

The rider's remaining points are answered. That the measured 0.96 km clears the 0.8 km absolute limb is accepted, but POL-RD-01 requires both limbs and the relative limb fails. That the rider was billed 17.0 km rather than the 16.0 km itinerary is not a billing defect: the meter charges the distance actually driven (16.96 km, rounded to 17.0 km), and the matched itinerary is the comparator for the deviation test, not a cap on the bill. The driver's profile decided nothing either way: no material deviation arises (6.00% is far below 50% and 0.96 km far below 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 check is not engaged and no conduct referral or uplift follows; and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d of 0 adds no corroboration burden under POL-RD-08.

Everything this ruling rests on carries weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-02860 and EV-GPS-02860), so confidence is not discounted, and the missing advisory at weight 0.0 carries no fact. The monetary effect is nil, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal it once under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

To the rider and the driver: both of you agree on the arithmetic, and so do I, so this is a short case on the money and a longer one on the defences.

THE FINDING. The measurement that governs is the GPS trace, EV-GPS-02858: 27.69 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off, against the booked optimal route of 21.3 km on EV-TRIP-02858 (POL-RD-01 says the trace figure governs over the rounded 27.7 km copy on the trip record). That is 6.39 km and 30.0% over. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (not more than 50%, not more than 8.0 km), and the trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 218 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged.

THE MONEY. The fare model on EV-FARE-02858 is METERED, so POL-RD-02 applies. Taking the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on that same artifact (1.0, read from nowhere else): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.3 + 0.28 x 28.8) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 28.639. charged_total was 35.52. Refund = 35.52 - 28.639 = 6.881, above the 0.50 de minimis and 19.4% of the charge — far below the 90% that would make it a full refund — so the payable amount, rounded up to the nearest 0.05, is 6.90. Nothing is added on top: there are no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09(1) forbids any add-on and POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line to correct. The rider asked for 6.90 rather than the 9.00 on the dispute form, and 6.90 is the whole of the remedy; the claim for the balance is not supported by any clause.

THE DRIVER'S DEFENCES. The chat log EV-CHAT-02858 is empty (0 messages), so POL-RD-04 has no rider instruction to work with and no waypoint_hint to test; the trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run. The only explanation offered is 'Followed navigation'. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02858-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 (an assertion that cites no artifact discharges nothing). Because no advisory was cited by the driver, POL-RD-13(1) applies: an uncited traffic assertion is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, so the case is ruled and not escalated, and POL-RD-13(2) leaves the deviation standing at the measured figure.

THE IDENTIFIER POINT (the driver's two alternative arguments). I have checked it. EV-FARE-02858 is filed under this trip's identifier TRP-02858; its line is charged at 09:17:49, 25 seconds after this trip's ended_at of 09:17:24, for exactly the 35.52 in dispute, and its charged distance and time (27.7 km, 36.2 min) match the trip record. The string 'TRP-02758' inside its payload is contradicted by the rest of that same artifact. The three artifacts do carry matching trip identifiers, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged and POL-RD-10(2) does not fire. I record the inconsistency here rather than in the referrals list: no clause produces a referral for it, and the platform should correct the ledger payload so the artifact reconciling to this trip reads TRP-02858 throughout. For completeness, no other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trace is unimpaired (10(3)), the money is nowhere near the 10(6) ceiling, the timestamps cohere (10(4)), and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record (10(8)).

REPEAT-DEVIATION UPLIFT AND CONDUCT REFERRAL. None is available. The deviation is not material, so the POL-RD-06 check is not even triggered, and on its own test the driver's trailing-90-day figures on EV-DPROF-02858 (1 deviation flag, 309 completed trips) fall far below both the 3-flag and the 0.05-ratio thresholds. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and has not been used.

OUTCOME AND NEXT STEPS. The rider is refunded 6.90; the driver is owed nothing — the ledger billed 27.7 km against a trace of 27.69 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall under POL-RD-04. The confidence cap is set by the artifacts carrying the deciding facts (EV-GPS-02858, EV-TRIP-02858 and EV-FARE-02858, all at weight 1.0); the missing advisory carries no fact and does not cap it. The monetary effect (6.90) is below the 8.00 execution threshold, so it is released on issue. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
